phases.title: Layout and staging (still frame, no motion)
phases.goal: Master all eight layout systems from Kimberly Elam's Typographic Systems — axial, radial, dilatational, random, grid, modular, transitional, bilateral — as fluently readable, buildable compositions. Added as a stated goal 2026-09-23.
lessons: Pick a still from the reference pack. Direct a layout with the same weight distribution, different words.
Same layout, direct it with the anchor moved. What changes about what the frame means?
Direct a frame with deliberate negative space — where nothing is, on purpose.
Direct two versions of the same words: one centered/stable, one off-balance/tense. Name the emotional difference.
Pull one beat from the Inception script. Direct its layout as a still frame — no motion — before touching timing.

phases.title: Storyboarding (director-level planning)
lessons: Take one scene from the Inception script. Write a beat table: time code, VO line, mood direction, visual description.
Get a storyboard.html built from that beat table. Review it as a static contact sheet before anything moves.
Revise the beat table based on what the storyboard showed.
Lock one storyboard — this becomes the plan for Phase 4's build.

phases.title: Kinetic typography — when to use what
lessons: Pick two clips from the reference pack using different reveal moves on similar material. Fill in a row of the decision table from what you observe.
Pull 'He says: I do this for the money.' (Scene 2). Decide the right move using the decision table, and direct it.
Pull 'Mal keeps appearing.' (Scene 4). Direct it with the move the table says is wrong, on purpose — confirm it actually hurts.
Pull 'Once you see it, the heist stops being the point' (Scene 3) — a line that changes register mid-sentence. Decide one move or two, and direct it.
Assign a move to every line of one full beat using only the table, no new decisions. Time yourself.

phases.title: Motion as direction (timing and weight)
lessons: Direct the arrival of 'Mal.' — describe the feeling (intrusive? inevitable?), review variations, judge which is true.
Direct 'home' (Scene 3) two ways — heavy and weightless. Same words, only the feeling changes.
Direct the anticipation beat for 'the money' (Scene 2) — pull back before the reveal.
Direct one full transition: the match cut described in the Story Dojo notes (surface claim → deeper pattern).
Take the locked storyboard and Phase 3's type-move decisions. Direct motion for each beat in sequence — first assembled candidate.

phases.title: Space and camera — the director's vocabulary for 3D
lessons: Take one Phase 4 beat. Decide: does this need depth, or does a flat frame already serve it? If flat serves it, log that and stop.
For a beat that needs it: direct the same framing at two lens choices (wide vs. long). Name the emotional difference.
Direct the same shot at three camera heights. Name the power relation each implies.
Direct a reveal using fog/depth-of-field instead of a cut or mask.
Direct one real Inception beat in depth, only if session 1 confirmed it earns the dimension.
